talk: A waterfall sets the order in which a fund's money is paid out. Investors get their money back first, then a preferred return (often 8%), and only after that do the managers share in the profit. Real waterfalls usually add a catch-up step, and this is the simple version.

terms.meaning: Investors get the money they put in back first.
The minimum return investors get before managers earn carry, often 8%.
The order money flows out of a fund.

questions.prompt: Investors put $100M into a fund with an 8% hurdle. How much must they get back before the managers earn any carry?
questions.hint: Their money back plus the hurdle.
whyNot: $8M is just the hurdle. Investors get their $100M back first too.
$100M only returns their money. The 8% hurdle comes first as well.
$180M is far too much. The hurdle is $100M x 8% = $8M, so investors need $100M + $8M = $108M.

questions.prompt: The fund returns $158M. How much is left after investors get their $108M?
questions.hint: Total minus what investors get first.
whyNot: $8M is the hurdle, already paid to investors.
$158M is the whole amount, before investors are paid.

questions.prompt: The managers take 20% of that $50M. How much carry do they get?
questions.hint: 20% of what's left after the hurdle.
working: Investors get the other $50M - $10M = $40M, so $108M + $40M = $148M in total.
whyNot: $158M - $100M = $58M of profit, and $58M x 20% = $11.6M takes carry on all of it. With a hurdle, the first $8M goes to investors only.
$40M is the investors' share of the $50M.
The managers get 20% of it, not all of it.

penalty.prompt: Investors put {fund} into a fund with a {hurdle} hurdle. The fund returns {back}. Managers take {carry} of what's left after investors get their money and the hurdle. How much carry?
penalty.hint: Investors first, then 20% of what's left.
working: Carry: {back - fund * (1 + hurdle)|usd} x {carry} = {(back - fund * (1 + hurdle)) * carry|usd}.

traps.why: That takes carry on all the profit. The hurdle goes to investors first.

call.title: The bonus pot
call.prompt: The club made $1M more profit than planned. The shareholder deal says owners first get an 8% return on the $5M they put in, then staff share 20% of anything above that.

options.label: Follow the waterfall
options.result: Good call. Owners first: $5M x 8% = $400,000. Above that: $1M - $400,000 = $600,000, and staff get $600,000 x 20% = $120,000.

options.label: Give staff 20% of the whole $1M
options.result: $1M x 20% = $200,000 skips the hurdle. The owners' 8% comes first.

options.label: Pay staff nothing this year
options.result: Breaking the deal saves $120,000 and costs you your best people.

later.text: Two key coaches leave after the bonus row. About 800 fans follow them out.

takeaway: Waterfall: money back, then the hurdle, then the profit split.
